Earlier this summer, Apple closed part of the Apple Park Visitor Center for "store improvements."

The space has since reopened, and the biggest change is that Apple has removed the augmented reality experience that let visitors use a custom iPad to explore Apple Park.

When the Apple Park Visitor Center opened in 2017, Apple described the AR experience this way:

"Experience a 3D model of the campus come to life through augmented reality, inviting visitors to explore Apple Park in an immersive, interactive way. Visitors can learn about the largest naturally ventilated building in the world, and see one of the largest on-site solar installations in the world. Visitors can also choose to lift the entire roof off the building to look at the layout of the collaborative workspaces inside."

Before this change, the Apple Park Visitor Center was divided into three sections: the AR exhibit, a traditional Apple Store, and a cafe.

Apple has now retired the AR exhibit and converted that space into an extension of the traditional Apple Store. As spotted by MacRumors, the renovation includes an Avenues accessories display wall, as well as redesigned Apple product display tables.

The rest of the Apple Park Visitor Center, including the cafe, remains unchanged.

9to5Mac Opinion

The AR experience at the Apple Park Visitor Center was certainly unique, but nine years on, the space seems like it could be put to better use.

I was hoping Apple would try something other than the AR experience, rather than turning it into another traditional retail store, but at least the cafe remains and is still one of the unique highlights of the Apple Park Visitor Center.
